title: The affine line and the punctured line over a base
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme,
and use the affine-line datum of [def-pur-affine-line-datum]: the
projection $p:\mathbf A^1_Y\to Y$, the zero section $s$, the open
complement $j:\mathbf G_{m,Y}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_Y$, the composite
$\pi=pj:\mathbf G_{m,Y}\to Y$, the finite-level twist
$\Lambda(1)=\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$, and the Kummer class
$\kappa(t)\in H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\Lambda(1))$ of the coordinate. Write
$R^m\pi_*=\mathcal H^m R\pi_*$ for the cohomology sheaves of
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Then:

1. *(Acyclicity of the affine line.)* The units
$\Lambda_Y\to Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}$ and
$\Lambda_Y(1)\to Rp_*\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)$ are isomorphisms; so
$R^mp_*\Lambda(1)=0$ for $m>0$.
1. *(The Kummer generator.)* The unit
$\Lambda_Y(1)\to R^0\pi_*\Lambda(1)$ — equivalently, restriction along $j$
composed with the pullback $p^*$ — is an isomorphism, and the map
$$
\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1),\qquad 1\longmapsto\kappa(t),
$$
sending $1$ to the image of $\kappa(t)$ under the edge map
$H^1(\mathbf G_{m,Y},\Lambda(1))=H^1(Y,R\pi_*\Lambda(1))\to
\Gamma(Y,R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1))$, is an isomorphism: $R^1\pi_*\Lambda(1)$
is free of rank one on $\kappa(t)$.
1. *(Vanishing above degree one.)* $R^m\pi_*\Lambda(1)=0$ for $m\geq2$.
1. *(Base change.)* For every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$ of separated
finite-type $k$-schemes, with base changes
$p':\mathbf A^1_{Y'}\to Y'$, $\pi':\mathbf G_{m,Y'}\to Y'$ and
$g':\mathbf G_{m,Y'}\to\mathbf G_{m,Y}$, the pullback of the Kummer class
is the Kummer class, $g'^*\kappa(t)=\kappa(t')$, and the base-change
morphisms
$$
g^*Rp_*\Lambda(1)\to Rp'_*\Lambda(1),\qquad
g^*R\pi_*\Lambda(1)\to R\pi'_*\Lambda(1)
$$
are isomorphisms.

The same base-change conclusion also holds for $g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point, without requiring $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ to be of finite type over $k$. Thus (1)–(3) can be checked on geometric fibres: over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ the affine line has only constant $H^0$, while the punctured line has constant $H^0$, $H^1$ freely generated by $\kappa(t)$, and no higher cohomology.

proof.text: Set $r=\ell^N$ and choose $\zeta$. [lem-pur-relative-kummer-coefficient-normalization] makes $A$ finite free over $\mathbf Z/r$, trivializes the twist naturally and fixes the module/abelian and Kummer pullback maps. Apply [thm-pur-kummer-affine-line] to obtain the absolute constants, Kummer generator and vanishings, with their specified maps.

proof.text: For $C=\mathbf A^1_k$ or $\mathbf G_{m,k}$ and any $k$-scheme $B$, [lem-pur-relative-kummer-strict-local-invariance] identifies $R\Gamma(C_S,L)$ with $R\Gamma(C,L)$ by the actual pullback for every strict localization $S$ of $B$. [lem-pur-relative-kummer-normalized-stalks] identifies the relative derived stalks through this map, preserving units and Kummer germs. Its conservative-stalk conclusion applied to step 1 gives clauses (1)–(3) over $B$, including untwisted acyclicity and restriction along $j$.

source.place: Step 2: strict-local comparison and geometric stalks

proof.text: For $g:B'\to B$, apply [lem-pur-relative-kummer-exchange-generators] with $L=A(1)_B$. Its unit identity gives degree zero; its edge identity carries the coordinate class to the pulled-back class, which is $\kappa(t')$ by [lem-pur-relative-kummer-coefficient-normalization]. Step 2 gives the required unit and generator isomorphisms and vanishings over both bases. The lemma's cohomological criterion proves that both specified etale exchange maps are invertible. This applies also to $B'=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, since neither step assumes finite type for $B$.

source.place: Step 3: unit and class compatibility for exchange

proof.text: Both projections are affine, hence qcqs, as are all their base changes. Apply [lem-pur-relative-kummer-site-normalization]: exact comparison transports the vanishings and actual units of step 2; its equality $c^1(\kappa_{\mathrm{et}})=\kappa$ identifies the actual pro-etale edge generator; and its conjugation identity transports the exchanges of step 3. Thus every clause holds in the prescribed pro-etale convention, including arbitrary geometric points. Pulling the coordinate pulls its Kummer class to $\kappa(t')$, so the fibre computations have the stated normalization.
